title: Storytelling
idea:
Hypothesis: the angle already wins; told as a brand mission, in a "we" voice, it can win in a second format.
WHY: #316 is our top spender (27% of last week's spend) with this angle: skin tags gone without the pain, blood and scar of the other methods. Today we only run it as a ranking / talking head.
WHAT: the same angle told as a brand-mission story, modelled on the Conscious Bar ad.
HOW: female voiceover, nobody on camera, one visual world, 3 visual hooks with the same voiceover.

script.script:
What's the worst part about having a skin tag?

I'll give you a hint. It's not how it looks.
script.visual: H1 THE BLADE (reference image attached; the second image is the Meta safe-zone guide). Extreme macro of a small skin tag on a woman's neck, lit like jewelry, deep green background. A small steel blade slowly enters from the right toward the tag and stops just short. Slow push-in. It never touches the skin.
script.on_screen_text: HOOK TITLE, fixed at the top for the first 5s: What's the worst part about having a skin tag? / Captions start below at "I'll give you a hint." Emphasis in gold: hint, how it looks.

script.script:
Same voiceover as H1: What's the worst part about having a skin tag?

I'll give you a hint. It's not how it looks.
script.visual: H2 THE COLLAGE (reference image attached). Paper cut-out collage on cream and deep green paper: the neck with the skin tag circled in gold. The title sits on the cream band at the top. The freezing can, the nail clippers, the floss and the invoice slide in one by one from the edges after the title, stop-motion feel, closing in on the neck.
script.on_screen_text: HOOK TITLE, fixed at the top for the first 5s, dark green on the cream band: What's the worst part about having a skin tag? / Captions start below at "I'll give you a hint." Emphasis in gold: hint, how it looks.

script.script:
Same voiceover as H1: What's the worst part about having a skin tag?

I'll give you a hint. It's not how it looks.
script.visual: H3 THE FREEZE (reference image attached). Same macro as H1, same neck and skin tag. The nozzle of a freezing applicator enters from the right with a puff of cold white vapor drifting toward the tag. It stops short and never touches the skin.
script.on_screen_text: HOOK TITLE, fixed at the top for the first 5s: What's the worst part about having a skin tag? / Captions start below at "I'll give you a hint." Emphasis in gold: hint, how it looks.

script.script: This is one. It's just a tiny piece of extra skin. It's totally harmless, and about half of all adults have them.
script.visual: Same macro neck as the hook, with no tools in frame: just the tiny skin tag, calm, lit like jewelry. Slow drift. On "about half of all adults": three quick macro cuts of other small tags (underarm, collarbone, eyelid) in the same warm light.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: harmless, half of all adults.

script.script: But somewhere along the way, getting rid of one turned into this.
script.visual: (Reference image attached; the caption on it belongs to the next line.) Hard cut to the green set: the instruments laid out on the deep green cloth like surgical tools. Freezing pen, nail clippers, knotted floss, the dermatologist bill behind. Slow push-in.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in red: this.

script.script: We freeze them. We cut them. We tie them off with floss. Or we pay a dermatologist a few hundred bucks, out of pocket, to burn them off. And yeah, that one works. It also leaves a scar.
script.visual: Same green set, one macro per sentence, each object alone on the cloth: the freezing pen releasing cold vapor; the nail clippers snapping shut; the floss pulled tight into a knot; the dermatologist bill sliding into frame next to a cautery pen. On "It also leaves a scar": the macro neck with a small pale round scar.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only (style: see the image on the row above). Emphasis in red: freeze, cut, tie, a few hundred bucks, burn, scar.

script.script: That's the worst part. Getting rid of it. It blisters. It bleeds. It swells. All for something that was never dangerous in the first place.
script.visual: (Reference image attached.) Macro neck, same framing as the hook, with a small round bandage and a faint pink flush around it. No blood, no wound. On "never dangerous in the first place": cut back to the calm macro of the tiny skin tag from the bridge.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in red: getting rid of it, blisters, bleeds, swells.

script.script: So we asked a simple question. What if you didn't have to attack it? What if you just rolled on one of the oldest skin remedies in the world?
script.visual: (Reference image attached.) A hand sweeps the instruments off the green cloth. Empty green for a beat. Then castor beans and a seed pod on the same cloth, and a thick golden drop of oil falls into a small pool.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: a simple question, skin remedies.

script.script: Cold-pressed castor oil.
script.visual: PRODUCT REVEAL, about 0:42: our real bottle held up in a woman's hand against the deep green backdrop, label to camera. Use the Products tab photos so the label stays exact.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: castor oil.

script.script: Would it actually work? Would it even budge? Or would it just suck?
script.visual: Macro on the same neck: the rose quartz roller ball, glistening with oil, next to the skin tag. One beat per question: it approaches, it pauses, it touches and rolls once.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in red: suck.

script.script: Well, it didn't. Castor oil soaks down to the root of the tag. So in a few weeks, the tag dries out, shrinks, and falls off on its own.
script.visual: Mechanism animation: reuse the #156 skin-tag animation (oil sinking to the root, the tag drying out and shrinking), the same one #316 uses, graded warm so it sits in this world. Then the macro neck with the tag visibly smaller.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: the root, a few weeks, falls off on its own.

script.script: No pain. No blood. No scar. Just smooth skin where it used to be.
script.visual: (Reference image attached.) The exact framing of hook H1, same neck: the skin tag is gone, the skin is smooth, her hair is pinned up. Hold the shot. This is the "after" of the hook.
script.on_screen_text: Captions, bigger than usual and stacked: No pain. / No blood. / No scar. (cream, last line in gold).

script.script: And one day you put your hair up and don't think twice about it.
script.visual: A little wider, from behind or the side, no face: her hands gather her hair up and pin it in one easy motion, neck fully exposed, deep green backdrop, same warm light.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: don't think twice.

script.script: Over 43,000 women already roll it on every night.
script.visual: SOCIAL PROOF. 3 or 4 very quick shots (about 1 second each) of different women, 45 to 60, each one rolling our bottle on her neck or collarbone and looking at the camera with a small relaxed smile.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: 43,000 women.

script.script: It's the first castor oil made just for skin tags. You don't pour it. You roll it, right on the base of the tag. Neck, underarms, bra line. Ten seconds before bed, and it works while you sleep.
script.visual: Macro of the roller ball rolling on the base of a skin tag. Then three quick macros in the same light: neck, underarm, bra line. The bottle is set down on a dark nightstand and the light dims.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: just for skin tags, roll it, while you sleep.

script.script: It's cold-pressed. No hexane. And it never touches plastic. You won't find that anywhere else on the shelf.
script.visual: Macro beauty shots on the green set, one per phrase: golden oil dripping; the amber glass catching the light; the rose quartz ball turning.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: cold-pressed, no hexane, never touches plastic.

script.script: That's what we're here for. No more freezing. No more cutting. No more burning.
script.visual: The instruments from the green set, one on each "No more": each is swept off the cloth or dropped into a drawer. Last beat: the empty green cloth.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in red: freezing, cutting, burning.

script.script: We truly believe that's the future of skin tag removal.
script.visual: Our bottle alone on the green cloth. Slow push-in, warm light, long soft shadow.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: the future.

script.script: This is Haven & Spool. Organic castor oil. Amber glass. A rose quartz roller. That's it.
script.visual: (Reference image attached.) Hero still life: our bottle in the centre with castor beans, a piece of raw rose quartz and a small pool of golden oil around it. Cut on each phrase: the beans and oil, the glass, the quartz.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: Haven & Spool.

script.script:
And we really want you to see it for yourself.

It's buy one, get one free through Black Friday. And if your skin tag's still there after 30 nights, you get your money back. Link's below.
script.visual: (Reference image attached.) Two of our bottles side by side on the green set, then the end card in brand colours (deep green, cream, gold) with the offer. A small arrow points down on "Link's below".
script.on_screen_text: END CARD: Buy 1, Get 1 Free / 30 nights or your money back / Link below

editing_notes:
VISUAL STYLE (see the reference images attached to the script rows; they show both the look of the shot and the text style). This is a brand film, not UGC. ONE WORLD from the first frame to the last: deep forest green cloth and backdrop (the green of our label), warm hard directional light, brass-gold highlights, amber glass, rose quartz pink. Objects and hands tell the story. Only two visual languages: (1) photographic macro and tabletop still life, the main one; (2) paper cut-out collage, as an accent (hook H2, optional for the "oldest skin remedies" beat). The attached images are style frames for inspiration
THE STORY IN OBJECTS: the villains are the freezing pen, the nail clippers, the floss and the dermatologist bill. The origin is castor beans and golden oil. The hero is our bottle, which first appears on "Cold-pressed castor oil." (about 0:42) and never before.

BOOKEND: the "smooth skin" shot repeats the exact framing of hook H1 (same neck, tag gone).

3 HOOKS = same voiceover, different first 5 seconds. H1 the blade, H2 the collage, H3 the freeze. The tools never touch the skin. No blood, no gore anywhere in the ad.


TEXT ON SCREEN (the attached images show exactly how it should look). Two layers, and only two:
1) CAPTIONS, the whole ad: the spoken words, two to five at a time, centred, clean sans-serif, white, no box. In each caption ONE key word or phrase is bigger and in colour: RED for the other methods and the damage, GOLD for our side. The Text Overlay column says which words to emphasise in each row.
2) HOOK TITLE, first 5 seconds only: the question "What's the worst part about having a skin tag?" in a cream serif, no box, fixed at the top of the safe zone. It appears first, alone. Do not repeat the question in the captions. The captions start underneath at "I'll give you a hint." and "It's not how it looks." At about 5 seconds the title leaves and only captions remain.
No other overlays. The only full-screen card is the END CARD with the offer.

LENGTH: about 1:45. Do not speed up the voice to shorten it.

END CARD: Buy 1 Get 1 Free + 30 nights or your money back, in brand colours (see the image on the CTA row). Landing page: Skin Tags (page A).

Voiceover: Female voice, American, 45-55, warm and a little dry-humoured. It must sound like a real woman telling a story to a friend, NOT an announcer and NOT an AI read. Natural pauses, small smiles in the voice, uneven rhythm. Conviction on the mission lines. Key delivery notes: (1) pause after "skin tag?" and again after "hint."; (2) "And yeah, that one works." is said as an honest aside; (3) "Or would it just suck?" is playful, then "Well, it didn't." is short and deadpan; (4) the closing line before the offer ("we really want you to see it for yourself") must be said with energy, almost laughing, or it sounds forced. Pronunciation: Haven & Spool = HAY-vin and SPOOL. If using ElevenLabs Voice Changer, record a real human read first and convert, so the pacing stays human.

Avatar: Desire: "I want my skin tags gone."
Who: women 45 to 65 in the US with skin tags on the neck, underarms or bra line.
Behavior (sub-avatar): she has already tried, or seriously looked at, a freezing kit, clipping it, tying it off with floss, or a dermatologist quote, and backed off because of the pain, the bleeding, the scar or a bill her insurance won't cover. So she keeps putting it off.
Belief holding her back: "Every way of getting rid of it hurts, scars or costs hundreds, so I just live with it."
Why she cares about this ad: it says out loud what really bothers her, which is the removal and not the look, and shows a way that doesn't attack the skin.
